title: Polished and Released my AI Game!
author: BandicootWide8250
selftext:
I've spent roughly a month making this game including prototyping, going back and forth with design decisions, and refining the aesthetic decisions slowly over time. The past 2 weeks has mostly been bug testing and slowly going down my planned feature list until I finally cleared it!

Game is made Godot and with Claude Code, mostly Opus 5.5 but a bit of Fable 5.2 when it released. Sounds were mostly bought or used with CC0 licenses, songs are ones that I made in Suno. The artwork was the most fun to mess with, and some of them have some small fixes/adjustments by me, but still mostly AI! In game shaders with Godot to make 3D props look mostly the part, Gemini for image generation for some sprites and textures, and using Meshy + a custom Harness with an integrated pipeline to take 3D models and animations on those models to convert them into sprites in every direction in the game for human/alien sprites! Once they are made into sprites, it also automatically forms a spritesheet, spaces every sprite appropriately, and hands it off to Claude who is able to cut them up and use them directly in Godot. Once that's ready, it's fairly trivial to add new sprites and animations into the game.

The promotional material, including the trailers is also mostly AI. I put together a few of the clips and picked out a few I wanted to show, with the gameplay itself being the in game AI playing some missions. 

I think the hardest part is still rigging and animations and it's been the hardest part for a while, which is why I originally went with this idea as it's much easier to hide/remove smaller imperfections with the animations when they are converted into sprites.

  
It's a mix of X-Com and Wolfenstein, originally was going for Doom but slowly crept a bit forward with the fidelity and features.

  
It's free to play and on itch under [nuclearviber.itch.io/invayyders](http://nuclearviber.itch.io/invayyders) if anyone would like to check it out or give any feedback to things they would like to see added!

comments.body: Looks like fun. The graphics remind me of (my age) but back in the day we had a SNES game called Contra. It was super sweet. This reminds of that game but in FPV. Super cool!!

comments.author: Arya_the_Gamer
comments.body: This one looks a lot similar to another game called Hamburger Hill that was also made with AI assistance. Looks fun just like that one.

replies.author: BandicootWide8250
replies.body: I saw that one! Looks very good as well! I do wonder if they are also using 3D models or not, I think our sprites look a tad different but it might be hard to tell

comments.author: BrainsVsBrawnVsBears
comments.body: This looks really fun! I think the idea of turning 3d models into sprites is really interesting. I ended up doing something similar for the web port game I’m working on. It’s cool because it avoids a lot of the pitfalls of getting a consistent look when animating

comments.author: boynet2
comments.body: looks nice, these days with all the AI cant you make it available to play online? I am not sure how many people can allow themself to download exe

replies.author: BandicootWide8250
replies.body: I could and it's possible, just wasn't what I was originally going for. Would require a lot more testing and optimizing, which I already did for this game
